title: Candidate Orbit: Activation Checklist & Interview Rubric
body:
Purpose: a compact, pragmatic playbook for converting offers into fast, measurable impact. This doc bundles three things we keep rebuilding: (1) hiring timeline and gating checklist, (2) a lightweight interview rubric tailored for infra/serving/runtime candidates, (3) first-90-day onboarding + mentor pairing checklist. Use as a candidate-facing attachment and internal interviewer cheat-sheet.

Scope and audience: hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, hiring committee for senior ICs and new managers transitioning from IC track. Not exhaustive compliance doc (see people-ops/compliance).

Quick goals: 
- Reduce time-to-offer acceptance to <= 7 business days for high-fit candidates.
- Ensure 1st-30 day impact framing with measurable signals (PR merged, infra regression triage, onboarding eval).
- Standardize rubric so hiring committee can compare across teams.

Hiring timeline (recommended):
- Week 0: Recruiter screen + share Candidate Orbit packet (this doc + team 30/60/90 + mentor intro).
- Week 1: Two technical loops (systems + code pair) + one culture/leadership chat.
- Week 2: Hiring committee debrief, reference check, offer draft.
- Week 2–3: Offer negotiation, acceptance, start-date confirmed, pre-boarding comms.

Pre-boarding checklist (rec to recruiter + hiring manager):
- Candidate packet sent (team goals, first tasks, infra access overview).
- Intro email from hiring manager with suggested reading + Slack channel invite.
- Hardware request made if applicable (GPU node account, mac/ubuntu image).
- Assign buddy and mentor (buddy = day-to-day, mentor = career alignment).

Interview rubric — 4 pillars (score 0–4 each). Minimal needed to pass: total >= 10/16 and no pillar = 0.
1) Systems & distributed reasoning (4): design of low-latency inference systems, KV cache tradeoffs, batching. Look for: capacity planning thinking, cache invalidation strategies, fallback behavior.
2) Code & debugging (4): pragmatic code reading / small pair-program. Look for: clear incremental approach, testability, deterministic reproduce steps.
3) Reliability & oncall (4): incident triage, postmortem hygiene, SLA tradeoffs. Look for: concrete examples, blameless PMs, measurable mitigations.
4) Collaboration & communication (4): cross-team alignment, written clarity, stakeholder management. For manager hires include 1–1 coaching examples.

Scoring notes (interviewer cheatsheet):
- 4 = exceptional: explains tradeoffs, gives concrete metrics or past deliverables, can scaffold a plan.
- 3 = solid: good answers, minor gaps but sound.
- 2 = borderline: attempts plausible options but lacks depth or measurable outcomes.
- 1 = weak: answers are vague, no examples.
- 0 = no evidence.

Sample screening questions (add to interview packet):
- Systems: "Describe a cache invalidation strategy you implemented and how you measured correctness and effect on latency/cost."
- Code pair: "Given a small toy tokenizer + KV cache stub, implement the cache lookup and eviction for prefix reuse. Focus on correctness and fast feedback."
- Reliability: "Walk me through an outage where a model variant mismatch caused errors — how did you detect, mitigate, and prevent recurrence?"
- Collaboration: "Describe a time you negotiated a rollout window with infra and product and how you balanced risk vs velocity."

Onboarding: day-by-day checklist (condensed)
- Day -1: welcome packet + SLACK invites + onboarding calendar (HR, SSO, Security).
- Day 0: team intro, office logistics, machine setup, quick repo map.
- Day 1–5: small first task (label: 'first-pr: local dev -> CI green'), pair with buddy daily 30m.
- Week 1: meet key cross-functional stakeholders (SRE, platform, product), read design docs for serving runtime.
- Week 2–4: 2nd task (instrumentation/metric fix) that produces measurable signal (dashboard + alert).
- Week 4–8: ownership of a micro-project (eg: optimize KV cache eviction logic for X workload) with weekly sync and mentor checkpoints.
- Week 9–13: ship rollout plan, complete post-ship retrospective, coach handover to team.

Success signals we report at 30/60/90:
- 30d: environment ready, first PR merged, buddy feedback positive, onboarding survey score >= 4/5.
- 60d: measurable contribution (perf improvement, bug fix reducing errors), cross-team contact list established.
- 90d: independent ownership of a small area, knowledge share delivered, manager recommends full autonomy.

Manager-specific additions:
- First 30 days: 1:1 with each direct report (sketch goals + baseline skill map), team health check, backlog triage.
- Manager interview add-on: leadership case (conflict resolution + hiring calibration example).

Documents to attach when sending to candidate:
- team-goals-90d.md, sample-30-60-90.pdf, mentor-guidelines.md (links included in recruiter packet).

Open questions / TODOs (working notes):
- Do we require a live demo for senior infra roles? (pros: deep signal; cons: candidate CV bias).
- Should rubric weights differ by level (senior vs staff)? proposal: same pillars, require higher threshold for staff (>=12).
- Create a short acceptance-email template for recruiters (place in /templates).

Acceptance email quick draft (for recruiter):
"Hi {name}, excited to extend Redwood Inference's offer for {role}. Attached: offer letter, candidate orbit packet (onboarding + mentor note), first-week plan. We'll follow up to confirm start date and hardware preferences. — {recruiter}"

Metrics to track (people-ops):
- time-to-offer, offer-accept rate, 30d retention, first-PR-to-merge time, onboarding-survey score.

Notes to self (informal):
- keep packet to 3 pages for candidate readability; lean on links for details.
- cross-check with legal on preboarding materials that mention specific infra (avoid prescriptive language).
- next iteration: add checklist for remote hires (timezone buddy overlap matrix).

Links & references: 
- internal: CONFLUENCE-ONBOARD-RT, Hiring Committee rubric canonical (link TBD)
- sample tasks: github.com/redwood-inference/new-hire-tasks

Revision history: 
- 2026-01-28: initial draft (Maya)
- 2026-02-10: added interview examples and scoring notes (Liam)
- 2026-03-02: refined onboarding milestones and metrics (Priya)

If you're reviewing: please comment inline in the doc, flag any blockers for legal or infra provisioning.

— Maya
